# 2011–12 Harvard Crimson Men's Basketball Team

## Overview

The 2011–12 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team represented Harvard University during the 2011–12 NCAA Division I basketball season. This was a historically significant season for the program.

## Key Achievement

This team won the **Ivy League championship**, which was notable as it marked Harvard's first NCAA Tournament appearance in 66 years (since 1946). This ended one of the longest NCAA Tournament droughts in college basketball.

## Coach

The team was coached by **Tommy Amaker**, who had been building the program since taking over in 2007.

## Notable Players

- **Keith Wright** - Senior forward and a key contributor
- **Kyle Casey** - Forward who was an important player for the team
- **Brandyn Curry** - Point guard
- **Laurent Rivard** - Sharpshooter known for three-point shooting

## NCAA Tournament

Harvard earned a #12 seed in the NCAA Tournament. They faced Vanderbilt in the first round but lost that game, ending their historic season.

## Significance

This season marked a turning point for Harvard basketball, establishing them as a competitive Ivy League program and beginning a period of sustained success in subsequent years.
